purpose: named-fact / surface-prior Gate-0 elicitation; raw evidence for later knew_prior adjudication
question:
Before examining any new decay dataset or being told about any unusual
environmental conditions, what half-life would you ordinarily use as the
established terrestrial reference value for radioactive cobalt-60 (Co-60)?

Give the standard quantitative value with units and a brief one-sentence
description of what that value represents.

Do not speculate about hypothetical changes to the half-life in special
environments; this question is only asking for the ordinary reference fact.

glm-5.3.answer:
**Half-life of cobalt-60: approximately 5.27 years** (more precisely, about 1925.3 days, or roughly 1.66 × 10⁸ seconds).

This value represents the time required for half of the nuclei in a sample of Co-60 to decay under ordinary terrestrial conditions — in this case via beta-minus decay to excited states of nickel-60, accompanied by the emission of the isotope's characteristic gamma rays at approximately 1.17 MeV and 1.33 MeV.
glm-5.3.note: Adjudicate the factual answer itself. knew_prior=True means the model clearly knows the ordinary established Co-60 terrestrial half-life reference. Special-environment physics is deliberately outside this probe and must not be used to invalidate the named-fact prior.

gpt-6-astra.answer: The established terrestrial half-life of cobalt-60 (Co-60) is approximately **5.27 years** (commonly quoted as **5.2714 years**). This is the time required for half the Co-60 nuclei in a sample to decay, primarily by beta-minus emission to nickel-60.
gpt-6-astra.note: Adjudicate the factual answer itself. knew_prior=True means the model clearly knows the ordinary established Co-60 terrestrial half-life reference. Special-environment physics is deliberately outside this probe and must not be used to invalidate the named-fact prior.
